will-gpt-6-be-released-by-august-31-2026.thesis_break_rule: CRITERIA RE-READ 2026-08-10 (21d to resolution, active Astra rumour flow). YES needs GPT-6 'made available to the GENERAL PUBLIC' by Aug-31 23:59 ET. The text is explicit that OPEN beta and OPEN ROLLING WAITLIST signups DO count, while a CLOSED beta or ANY form of private access does NOT, and the access must be 'clearly defined and publicly announced by OpenAI'. Naming: explicitly 'GPT-6' OR anything 'recognized as a successor to GPT-5' (so Astra can qualify on positioning alone); 'GPT-5.5 or similar' explicitly does NOT. => TIER-1 ALERT TRIAGE, decide BEFORE reacting: 'Astra waitlist opens' / 'generally available' / 'rolling access' = REAL thesis break, exit. 'Astra closed beta' / 'early access for select customers' / 'safety testing with partners' = NOT a break, hold — the criteria exclude private access by name. Current world state supports NO: Altman ~Aug-6 stated publicly that Astra is NOT yet generally available and that OpenAI needs 'a little longer' pending cyber-capability safety work — a dated first-party statement that the qualifying event has not occurred and is gated on a review. Prior 0.82 vs market 0.78 = 4pp, inside divergence threshold, no trade.
